subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the fixed 8192 MB generated service default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, requiring a tunable heap surface first, or switching to the CLI-argument approach?
rationale: All viable fixes change managed service startup behavior, and repository policy treats daemon defaults, config/env surfaces, and upgrade behavior as maintainer-owned compatibility decisions.

options.title: Land fixed default now
options.body: Accept the open PR as the narrow emergency mitigation, with follow-up tracking for a tunable heap-size surface if needed.

options.title: Require tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the open PR until maintainers choose and prove a CLI flag, config key, or durable service setting for low-memory and fleet-managed hosts.

options.title: Switch to CLI argument
options.body: Prefer the CLI-argument shape to avoid generating NODE_OPTIONS, then require repair of downstream argv assumptions and real daemon install proof.

recommendation.title: Land fixed default now
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR as the narrow emergency mitigation, with follow-up tracking for a tunable heap-size surface if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for the daemon install and service-startup paths points to steipete, and the decision is about the product/security tradeoff of that shared service boundary.
